Format a Temporal value as an ISO 8601 string

Source: R/temporal.R, R/duration.R, R/instant.R, and 6 more
temporal_to_string.Rd

Temporal's toString(). format() takes the same options and as.character() gives the default strings. Years outside 0 to 9999 are written with a sign and six digits. By default a time's fraction keeps only its significant digits, and a UTC offset is written as +HH:MM or -HH:MM, rounded to the minute (design 9).

Usage

temporal_to_string(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_duration'
temporal_to_string(
  x,
  ...,
  fractional_second_digits = "auto",
  smallest_unit = NULL,
  rounding_mode = "trunc"
)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_instant'
temporal_to_string(
  x,
  ...,
  fractional_second_digits = "auto",
  smallest_unit = NULL,
  rounding_mode = "trunc",
  time_zone = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_date_time'
temporal_to_string(
  x,
  ...,
  fractional_second_digits = "auto",
  smallest_unit = NULL,
  rounding_mode = "trunc",
  calendar_name = "auto"
)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_date'
temporal_to_string(x, ..., calendar_name = "auto")

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_month_day'
temporal_to_string(x, ..., calendar_name = "auto")

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_time'
temporal_to_string(
  x,
  ...,
  fractional_second_digits = "auto",
  smallest_unit = NULL,
  rounding_mode = "trunc"
)

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_plain_year_month'
temporal_to_string(x, ..., calendar_name = "auto")

# S3 method for class 'zutempo_zoned_date_time'
temporal_to_string(
  x,
  ...,
  fractional_second_digits = "auto",
  smallest_unit = NULL,
  rounding_mode = "trunc",
  calendar_name = "auto",
  time_zone_name = "auto",
  offset = "auto"
)

Arguments

x

A zutempo value.

...

Must be empty.

fractional_second_digits

"auto" (the default) for the significant digits of the fraction, or 0 to 9 for exactly that many.

smallest_unit

NULL (the default), or the smallest unit to write: "minute" (not for a duration), "second", "millisecond", "microsecond" or "nanosecond". It wins over fractional_second_digits.

rounding_mode

How a value is rounded to the precision: "trunc" (the default) or another of the nine Temporal modes, as in temporal_round().

time_zone

For an instant(): a time zone to show the time in, "UTC", a fixed offset such as "+05:30", an IANA identifier such as "Europe/Lisbon", or an ISO string that names one; NULL (the default) writes the time in UTC with Z.

calendar_name

Whether to write the [u-ca=iso8601] annotation: "auto" (the default) and "never" leave it out, "always" writes it, "critical" writes it with the ! flag. A year-month or month-day written with the annotation also shows its reference day or year.

time_zone_name

For a zoned_date_time(): "auto" (the default) writes the time zone annotation, "never" leaves it out, "critical" writes it with the ! flag.

offset

For a zoned_date_time(): "auto" (the default) writes the UTC offset, "never" leaves it out.

Value

A character vector, NA where x is NA.

Details

Each type takes the options its Temporal toString() has: the precision options on the types with a time, calendar_name on the types with a date, and time_zone_name and offset on a zoned_date_time(). A value rounded by smallest_unit or fractional_second_digits is rounded before it is written: a time wraps past midnight, a date-time moves to the next day, and a duration rounds its time part only.

Examples

temporal_to_string(plain_date(c(2026, 275760), c(1, 9), c(31, 13)))
#> [1] "2026-01-31"    "+275760-09-13"
temporal_to_string(instant("2026-01-31T12:30Z"), time_zone = "+05:30")
#> [1] "2026-01-31T18:00:00+05:30"
temporal_to_string(plain_time(12, 30, 45, 500))
#> [1] "12:30:45.5"
temporal_to_string(plain_time("23:59:59.987"), fractional_second_digits = 1)
#> [1] "23:59:59.9"
temporal_to_string(
  plain_date_time("2026-01-31T12:30:45.5"),
  smallest_unit = "second",
  rounding_mode = "halfExpand",
  calendar_name = "always"
)
#> [1] "2026-01-31T12:30:46[u-ca=iso8601]"
format(duration("PT1M30.25S"), smallest_unit = "second", rounding_mode = "ceil")
#> [1] "PT1M31S"
